newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Qantas sees aggressive response to any Ansett deal.
newsitem.headline: Qantas sees aggressive response to any Ansett deal.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd on Thursday threatened an aggressive response to what it called an imminent equity partnership between Singapore Airlines Ltd and Ansett Airlines.
"I can't predict our attitude towards it, other than it will be aggressive," Qantas chief executive James Strong told reporters.
Newspaper reports this week said Singapore Airlines Ltd is in preliminary talks to become an equal partner with News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd in regional operator Ansett Holdings Ltd.
Strong declined to comment further but said the deal was being arranged to give Ansett more coverage in the Asian market and elsewhere.

He said the deal was likely to require Foreign Investment Review Board approval and also the sanction of Australia's anti-monopolies authority as well as aviation regulator, the International Air Services Commission.
"As for Qantas, we do have very good connections into the Asian market and through the Asian market," Strong said.
He confirmed Qantas considered from time to time the merits of tying up with another Asian airline but any link between Singapore Airlines and Ansett would not add any impetus to this.
"I don't have a rabbit that I'm about to pull out of my hat on that," he said.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Aiways.
